patches.anchor: In the chapter “Bhagia and Saria” of ଛମାଣ ଆଠଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha), Fakir Mohan Senapati’s narrator turns towards educated readers who know distant societies better than their neighbours. The question is deliberately ironic:
patches.heading: Fakir Mohan Senapati: writing and circulation
patches.markdown: Fakir Mohan Senapati worked as a teacher and an administrator. His literary life also involved printing: Ramakanta Rout records his bringing a press from Calcutta to Balasore in 1868. Making words available belonged beside writing them.[^book-fakir-life]
notes: [^book-fakir-life]: Ramakanta Rout, [Vyasakavi Fakirmohan Senapati](https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/Orissareview/2010/April/engpdf/14-17.pdf), Odisha Review, April 2010, pp. 14–17.

patches.anchor: [Pratibha Ray](https://projectodisha.org/people/pratibha-ray/)’s official bibliography identifies her novel ଅପରିଚିତା (Aparichita) as adapted into a film and the title story of ମୋକ୍ଷ (Moksha) as adapted into a feature.[^pratibha] *Moksha* was directed by Gouri Shankar Das and Malaya Kumar Roy, with Das writing the screenplay. It received the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia for 1995.[^moksha-credits] A novel’s sustained companionship and a short story’s concentrated moment offer different possibilities to the screen.
patches.heading: Pratibha Ray: a working life beside the fiction
patches.markdown: Pratibha Ray’s professional account traces a life in teaching, from schools to government colleges. She retired voluntarily as a Professor of Education in 1998.[^book-ray-career] The work of education sits beside her fiction, whose journeys into performance take several forms.

patches.heading: Jatindra K. Nayak: a voice reconsidered
patches.markdown: Nayak describes narrative tone and culturally rooted characters as challenges for translation. He also says he would revisit his published translations: the work remains provisional.[^book-nayak-craft] Keeping his name beside Basanta’s lets readers recognise that continuing work.
notes: [^book-nayak-craft]: Pramod Kumar Das, [*Translation Today* 15(2), 2021](https://www.ntm.org.in/download/ttvol/volume15-2/Translations%201.pdf), p. 271; reproducing Nayak’s 2020 interview answer.

patches.anchor:
Producer [Deependra Samal](../../people/deependra-samal.md), co-director [Vishal Mourya](../../people/vishal-mourya.md) and co-director and editor [Debi Prasad Lenka](../../people/debi-prasad-lenka.md) brought different responsibilities to the film.[^producer-credit][^catalogue]

Their profiles follow the backing, writing and editing of the film. Its story also involves local performers, technicians and the healthcare workers who inspired it.
patches.heading_existing: The people who brought it together
patches.markdown:
### Vishal Mourya: learning to work together

Mourya recalled leaving software work after studying engineering, then finding his way into filmmaking. He met editor Debi Prasad Lenka on a television project in 2010. Their collaboration made room for disagreement: they discussed shots together and worked through roughly ten drafts of *DAMaN* before filming.[^book-mourya-journey]

### Debi Prasad Lenka: from voices to the edit

Lenka recalled a fifteen-day workshop before filming, during which preparation helped the team revise dialogue and translate passages spoken by tribal characters.[^book-lenka-workshop] He also edited the film.[^catalogue] His contribution connects the words prepared for performance with the work of assembling its finished form.

### Deependra Samal: a producer in the conversation

Samal produced the film under JP Motion Pictures.[^producer-credit] Mourya recalled his encouragement to make something distinctive.[^making] The directors also credited him with constructive feedback and an understanding of the project’s needs.[^book-samal-conversation]

These responsibilities met the work of local performers, technicians and the healthcare workers who inspired the film.
notes: [^book-mourya-journey]: Anish Mohanty, [interview with Vishal Mourya](https://planetbollywood.com/wp/interviews/i-am-hoping-the-hindi-version-of-daman-gets-a-lot-of-love-from-the-audience-vishal-mourya/), Planet Bollywood, ahead of the February 2023 Hindi release.

[^book-lenka-workshop]: [The Federal, interview with Debi Prasad Lenka and Vishal Mourya](https://thefederal.com/entertainment/its-not-just-kantara-odia-film-daman-is-making-waves-nationwide-meet-the-directors), December 2022, Lenka’s workshop answer; indexed interview. Translators unnamed.

[^book-samal-conversation]: [The Federal, interview with Debi Prasad Lenka and Vishal Mourya](https://thefederal.com/entertainment/its-not-just-kantara-odia-film-daman-is-making-waves-nationwide-meet-the-directors), December 2022. Indexed interview text.
